Chapter 7: Trusting Through Uncertainty and Fear
If you think about it, uncertainty is something we all bump into sooner or later. It sneaks in with all those questions about what’s next, worries about what could go sideways, and that uneasy sense that maybe things just won’t work out. When life feels unpredictable, trust can seem like this fragile hope—something that’s easy to lose when the future looks cloudy.
Picture a man standing at a crossroads in his life, having to decide whether to move his family for a new job. The fear? Absolutely real. The risks just kept piling up in his mind, each scenario playing out over and over, making it hard to breathe, let alone sleep. One night, restless and wide awake, he stepped outside and stared up at the stars. The sky was enormous, and suddenly, his problems didn’t seem quite so overwhelming. In that quiet moment, he felt a gentle sense of assurance—like maybe, just maybe, he wasn’t facing all this uncertainty on his own.
And honestly, most of us don’t even realize how much fear shapes our decisions. If you look back at stories from long ago—people facing impossible odds, leaving everything familiar behind, or stepping straight into the unknown—it wasn’t because they never felt afraid. What made them different was their willingness to trust, even when fear was right there with them.
Take a young woman who’s just graduated, for example. She’s staring down endless choices and feeling buried by expectations—her own and everyone else’s. She tries to map out every step, but nothing is certain. Then, over coffee with a friend, it hits her: she doesn’t need to have all the answers lined up. She realizes that trust isn’t about having every detail figured out—it’s about believing she won’t have to face what comes next alone.
The real breakthrough? Understanding that trust isn’t just a feeling—it’s a choice. It’s about deciding to move forward, even when you can’t see the whole path ahead. It’s so tempting to wait for everything to feel certain before making a move, but the real invitation is to step out anyway, trusting that guidance will come, one step at a time.
The God who whispers our names never says the journey will be free from uncertainty. The promise isn’t about everything going smoothly—it’s about presence. That steady hand when life spins out of control, that quiet voice when the storm is raging. So, if you’re facing fear right now, maybe the challenge isn’t to control every outcome, but to let go just a little—and rest in the assurance that, truly, you are not alone.
